name: PixiTween Director S8b: deploy, limits and responsive pass
description: Everything needed to ship one small container: rate limits and an upload limit appended to the middleware chain (limits read from the validated env), Dockerfile, fly.toml, a pre-deploy check, theme tokens and a responsive pass, and owner-run commands with teardown. No story runs docker or fly; the owner deploys.

readFirst: docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md (shared types, file ownership, repo rules)
docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/contract-issues.md (which gaps the contract update resolved; the one named shared edit)
docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md sections 2 (middleware.ts), 5 (GET /api/health is an S2 route) and 6 (D-8 env keys)
server/http/middleware.ts, server/http/auth.ts and server/http/static.ts (S2) before editing the chain
docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md section 5.8 (film admission: sizing from the Meta key's 150-requests-per-window limit) and docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md D-16
extraGuardrails: No story builds an image, runs docker or fly, or contacts any host; Dockerfile and fly.toml are checked as text.
Do not edit panel components owned by other steps for the responsive pass; fix with global CSS and list blockers in notes.

Shared edits (metadata.sharedEdits) are allowed only where a story names them and says exactly what is added: appending entries to middleware.ts, one stylesheet import in main.tsx, a start script in package.json if missing, and a minimal fix in static.ts; record each in notes.

Read FILMS_PER_HOUR_PER_IP, GENERATE_MAX_PER_HOUR, MAX_UPLOAD_MB, TRUST_FLY_CLIENT_IP and DATA_DIR from the validated env object (06 D-8) through server/http/limits-config.ts; never read process.env for them and never edit server/env.ts.

Film admission (US-015 to US-017): read FILMS_IN_FLIGHT_MAX, FILMS_QUEUE_MAX, FILMS_STARTS_PER_WINDOW and FILMS_WINDOW_SEC only through server/http/limits-config.ts. Install the queue only through the boot hook (replacing deps.admission); never edit S2's createDirectAdmission, S3b's films handler or routes.ts. The two named shared edits for this feature are one appended entry in server/boot.ts and one import plus one line in web/src/panels/Storyboard.tsx.
manualGates: MG-2 (owner): approve the hosting cost, then follow deploy/README.md (create app, volume, secrets, deploy). Smoke the live URL logged out: gallery loads (newest first), ?film=<id> replays, a new film works with the passcode, the 4th creation within an hour from one IP gets a 429, /api/health (an S2 route) answers without the passcode, an SSE stream stays open for 5 minutes, and films survive a machine restart (DATA_DIR on the volume).
MG-2b (owner): at 375 px there is no horizontal scroll on the live URL; light and dark themes are readable.
MG-3 (owner): on or after Mon 16 Nov 2026 run the teardown commands and confirm fly apps list and fly volumes list show nothing for this app.

MG-2c (owner, queue): with the passcode and FILMS_PER_HOUR_PER_IP raised for the test, start 7 films within a minute on the live URL: 2 run, 4 show 'Waiting for the crew' with positions 1 to 4, the 7th gets 429 busy; queued films start as slots and the start window free up; no film fails with a Meta 429. Read x-ratelimit-remaining-requests (one 1-token chat call) before and after one finished film to check the 40-requests-per-film budget and adjust FILMS_STARTS_PER_WINDOW / FILMS_WINDOW_SEC (design 5.8).

steps: Read server/env.ts (S2) to learn the validated env object and its accessor name, and docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 6 D-8: FILMS_PER_HOUR_PER_IP (default 3), GENERATE_MAX_PER_HOUR (4), MAX_UPLOAD_MB (25), TRUST_FLY_CLIENT_IP (false) and DATA_DIR are validated in env.ts. Create server/http/limits-config.ts exporting interface Limits { filmsPerHourPerIp: number; generateMaxPerHour: number; maxUploadMb: number; trustFlyClientIp: boolean; filmsInFlightMax: number; filmsQueueMax: number; filmsStartsPerWindow: number; filmsWindowSec: number } and getLimits(env?: <the env object type>): Limits that maps the validated env keys to these fields. With FILMS_PER_HOUR_PER_IP 1, GENERATE_MAX_PER_HOUR 2, MAX_UPLOAD_MB 5 and TRUST_FLY_CLIENT_IP true the same fields are 1, 2, 5 and true
limits-config.ts contains no reference to process.env

With the documented defaults getLimits also returns filmsInFlightMax 2, filmsQueueMax 4, filmsStartsPerWindow 3 and filmsWindowSec 300; with FILMS_IN_FLIGHT_MAX 1, FILMS_QUEUE_MAX 0, FILMS_STARTS_PER_WINDOW 2 and FILMS_WINDOW_SEC 60 they are 1, 0, 2 and 60

stories.title: In-memory sliding-window rate limiter
stories.description: As an operator, I want a small tested rate limiter so that one visitor cannot burn the demo's budget.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md section 5.7.

Create server/http/rate-limit.ts exporting createRateLimiter(opts: { windowMs: number; max: number; now?: () => number }) returning { check(key: string): { allowed: boolean; remaining: number; retryAfterSec: number }; peek(key: string): { allowed: boolean; remaining: number; retryAfterSec: number }; size(): number; sweep(): void }.

Implementation: Map<string, number[]> of accepted timestamps. check() drops timestamps older than now - windowMs, allows when fewer than max remain (recording the timestamp and returning remaining = max - count), otherwise denies without recording and returns retryAfterSec = ceil((oldest + windowMs - now) / 1000). peek() answers the same question as check() (what check would return now) without recording a timestamp; sweep() deletes keys whose arrays are empty after pruning; size() returns the number of keys.
Create server/http/rate-limit.test.ts with an injected clock.
acceptance: With max 3 and windowMs 3600000, calls at t=0, 1000 and 2000 are allowed with remaining 2, 1 and 0
The 4th call at t=3000 is denied with retryAfterSec 3597, and repeated denied calls do not extend the window
At t=3600001 the key is allowed again; different keys do not affect each other
After the clock passes every window, sweep() makes size() return 0
peek() never consumes budget: with max 1, peek at t=0 is allowed, check at t=0 is allowed with remaining 0, and peek at t=1 is denied

stories.title: Client IP helper that trusts Fly only when told to
stories.description: As an operator, I want a client IP helper so that rate limits key on the real visitor and spoofed headers cannot dodge them.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md section 5.7 (Fly-Client-IP is trustworthy only when nothing else sits in front of Fly; X-Forwarded-For is spoofable; getConnInfo comes from @hono/node-server/conninfo and remote.address may be undefined).

Create server/http/client-ip.ts exporting clientIp(c: Context, opts?: { trustFlyHeader?: boolean }): string and hashIp(ip: string): string. The default for opts.trustFlyHeader is getLimits().trustFlyClientIp.

clientIp: when opts.trustFlyHeader (default: getLimits().trustFlyClientIp from server/http/limits-config.ts) is true and the 'fly-client-ip' header is non-empty return it trimmed; otherwise try getConnInfo(c).remote.address inside try/catch (it throws outside @hono/node-server) and return it, or 'unknown'. Never read x-forwarded-for.
hashIp returns the first 8 hex characters of the sha256 of the ip (node:crypto), used in logs so raw addresses are not stored.
Create server/http/client-ip.test.ts using app.request with headers.
acceptance: With trustFlyHeader true and header Fly-Client-IP '203.0.113.7' the helper returns '203.0.113.7'
With trustFlyHeader false the same header is ignored and the helper returns 'unknown' under app.request (no connection info); an X-Forwarded-For header never changes the result
hashIp('203.0.113.7') returns 8 lowercase hex characters and the same value on every call, and differs from hashIp('203.0.113.8')

stories.title: Film-creation rate limit middleware
stories.description: As an operator, I want at most 3 new films per visitor per hour so that the live demo cannot be drained.
steps: Read server/http/rate-limit.ts, server/http/client-ip.ts and docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md sections 5.7 and 7.

Create server/http/film-limit.ts exporting createFilmLimit(deps?: { limiter?: ReturnType<typeof createRateLimiter>; max?: number; log?: (line: string) => void }): MiddlewareHandler. It applies only to method POST on exactly '/api/films'. The default max is getLimits().filmsPerHourPerIp (server/http/limits-config.ts); windowMs is one hour; the key is clientIp(c).
When denied respond 429 with JSON { error: 'rate_limited', retryAfterSec } and a Retry-After header, and log '[rate-limit] key=<hashIp> path=/api/films window=<n>/<max>'. Otherwise call next().
Create server/http/film-limit.test.ts with an injected limiter or clock.
acceptance: The first 3 POST /api/films requests from one IP reach the next handler; the 4th returns 429 with a JSON error 'rate_limited' and a Retry-After header
GET /api/films and POST /api/films/abc/chat are never counted or limited
With max 1 injected through deps the second POST is denied, and with no injected max the limit equals getLimits().filmsPerHourPerIp
The log line contains the hashed key and never the raw IP

stories.title: Generate-approval edge cap middleware
stories.description: As an operator, I want a coarse cap on generate approvals so that a burst cannot spend Clippy credits even if another check fails.

When denied respond 429 JSON { error: 'generate_cap', retryAfterSec } with Retry-After. Otherwise next().
Create server/http/generate-cap.test.ts.
acceptance: Four approve requests across different films and scenes pass and the 5th returns 429 with error 'generate_cap'
POST /api/films/f1/scenes/s1/mode and GET on the approve path are not counted
With max 2 injected through deps the 3rd approve request returns 429

stories.title: Upload size limit middleware
stories.description: As an operator, I want oversized uploads rejected early so that a large file cannot exhaust the small machine.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md sections 5.7 and 11 (V4): Hono's bodyLimit from 'hono/body-limit' checks Content-Length first and counts the stream when it is absent.

Create server/http/upload-limit.ts exporting createUploadLimit(opts?: { maxMb?: number }): MiddlewareHandler built on bodyLimit({ maxSize, onError }). maxMb defaults to getLimits().maxUploadMb (server/http/limits-config.ts). It applies only to POST on exactly '/api/films'; onError returns 413 JSON { error: 'payload_too_large', maxMb }.
Create server/http/upload-limit.test.ts with createUploadLimit({ maxMb: 1 }) on a test app that has a POST /api/films handler returning 200.
acceptance: A POST /api/films with a 2 MB body returns 413 and JSON error 'payload_too_large' with maxMb 1
A POST /api/films with a 100 KB body reaches the handler and returns 200
A 2 MB POST to another path such as /api/films/abc/chat is not limited by this middleware

steps: Read server/http/middleware.ts and server/http/auth.ts (S2) and docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/contract-issues.md item C-8 (06 section 2: S8b appends rate limits as a named shared edit).

stories.title: server/http/film-queue.ts: films-in-flight cap, FIFO queue, start budget
stories.description: As an operator, I want the crew to run only as many films as the Meta key's 150-requests-per-window budget allows, and to queue the rest, so that a busy demo slows down instead of failing.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md section 5.8 (sizing and algorithm), docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 4 (FilmAdmission) and D-16, shared/ports.ts and server/http/rate-limit.ts (createRateLimiter with check and peek).

Create server/http/film-queue.ts exporting createFilmQueue(opts: {maxInFlight: number; maxQueued: number; startsPerWindow: number; windowMs: number; now?: () => number; setTimer?: (fn: () => void, ms: number) => unknown; clearTimer?: (h: unknown) => void; log?: (line: string) => void}): FilmAdmission & {dispose(): void}. State: a Set of running film ids, a FIFO array of {filmId, run}, a starts limiter = createRateLimiter({windowMs, max: startsPerWindow, now}) used with the single key 'starts', and at most one pending timer.

submit(filmId, run): if the film is already running or queued return its current state; if the queue is empty, running.size < maxInFlight and starts.peek('starts').allowed, call starts.check('starts'), start the run and return {state: 'running'}; else if queue.length < maxQueued push it and return {state: 'queued', position: queue.length, etaSec}; else return {state: 'rejected', retryAfterSec}. Starting a run means: add the id to running, call run() inside Promise.resolve().then(run), catch and log a rejection (never rethrow), and in finally remove the id and call pump().

pump(): while the queue is not empty and running.size < maxInFlight: const g = starts.check('starts'); if !g.allowed schedule one pump after g.retryAfterSec * 1000 ms through setTimer (replace any pending timer) and stop; else shift the head, start it. etaSec for a queued film at 1-based position p is p * ceil(windowMs / startsPerWindow / 1000) (an estimate: one start interval per film ahead of it plus its own); retryAfterSec for a rejection is max(ceil(windowMs / startsPerWindow / 1000), starts.peek('starts').retryAfterSec).

canAccept(): {ok: true} when queue.length < maxQueued, or when the queue is empty, a slot is free and starts.peek('starts').allowed; otherwise {ok: false, retryAfterSec} (same value as a rejection). position(filmId): running, queued with its 1-based position and etaSec, or unknown. stats(): inFlight, queued, maxInFlight, maxQueued, startsInWindow = startsPerWindow - starts.peek('starts').remaining, startsPerWindow and windowSec = windowMs / 1000. dispose() clears the timer.
Log one line per transition through opts.log: `[queue] film=<id> state=<running|queued|done|rejected> inFlight=<n>/<max> queued=<n>/<max> starts=<n>/<max>` (film ids only, no IPs).

Create server/http/film-queue.test.ts with an injected clock and a manual timer: maxInFlight 2, maxQueued 2, startsPerWindow 3, windowMs 300000. Submit a, b, c, d, e with runs that finish when the test resolves them: a and b return running, c is queued at position 1 (etaSec 100), d at position 2 (etaSec 200), e is rejected with retryAfterSec 100 and canAccept() is ok false; resolving a starts c (the third start in the window) and d moves to position 1; resolving b does not start d yet because four starts in 300 s are not allowed, a timer is pending, and after advancing the clock past 300000 ms and firing the timer d starts; FIFO order c before d; a run that rejects frees its slot and does not throw; submitting an id that is already running or queued returns its state without starting a second run; position() and stats() report the numbers above; dispose() clears the pending timer.
acceptance: With maxInFlight 2 and maxQueued 2, the first two submits run at once, the next two queue at positions 1 and 2, and the fifth is rejected with a retryAfterSec
No more than startsPerWindow films start inside one window even when slots are free; the waiting film starts after the window frees and a timer fires
Queued films start in FIFO order; a run that rejects releases its slot and never throws out of submit()
canAccept() is false exactly when submit() would reject

stories.title: server/http/film-queue-install.ts: boot hook, public queue reads, requeue after restart
stories.description: As an operator, I want the real queue installed at boot, with its state readable by the browser, and films waiting at a restart picked up again.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md D-3 (boot hooks), D-10 (entry points), D-16 and section 5 (GET /api/queue), server/boot.ts, server/admission.ts, server/http/limits-config.ts, server/http/film-queue.ts and, if present, server/agent/director.ts (bindDirector, runDirector; S3b).

Create server/http/film-queue-install.ts exporting createInstallFilmQueue(opts?: {loadDirector?: () => Promise<{bindDirector?: (deps: AppDeps) => void; runDirector?: (filmId: string) => Promise<void>}>; log?: (line: string) => void}): BootHook and `export const installFilmQueue = createInstallFilmQueue()`. The default loadDirector is `() => import('../agent/director')`.

The hook does, in order: read getLimits(); build the queue with createFilmQueue({maxInFlight: filmsInFlightMax, maxQueued: filmsQueueMax, startsPerWindow: filmsStartsPerWindow, windowMs: filmsWindowSec * 1000, log}); set deps.admission = queue (replacing S2's direct admission); register app.get('/api/queue', c => c.json(queue.stats())) and app.get('/api/queue/:filmId', c => c.json(queue.position(c.req.param('filmId')))) (public reads: the passcode middleware only guards mutating methods; set no CORS headers); then requeue: list deps.films.list(), keep films whose status is 'new', sort by createdAt ascending, and for each call queue.submit(film.id, () => runDirector(film.id)) after bindDirector(deps) when it exists; if loadDirector throws or runDirector is missing log '[queue] director not available; skipping requeue' and continue; log '[queue] requeued <n> film(s)'.
Edit server/boot.ts (a named shared edit: the file belongs to S2): add one import and append `installFilmQueue` to bootHooks, leaving every other entry unchanged; record the edit in notes.

Create server/http/film-queue-install.test.ts with a Hono app and fake deps (films with two 'new' films of different createdAt and one 'ready' film; a fake loadDirector whose runDirector records ids and never resolves): after the hook runs deps.admission.stats().maxInFlight equals getLimits().filmsInFlightMax; GET /api/queue returns the stats JSON with status 200 even when DIRECTOR_PASSCODE is set and no credentials are sent; GET /api/queue/<id> of a queued film returns {state: 'queued', position, etaSec} and of an unknown id {state: 'unknown'}; the two 'new' films are submitted oldest first and the 'ready' film is ignored; with a loadDirector that throws no film is submitted and the hook still completes; the hook is registered in bootHooks (import server/boot.ts and assert installFilmQueue is included).
acceptance: After the boot hook, handlers that call getAdmission(deps) get the real queue (stats().maxQueued equals getLimits().filmsQueueMax)
GET /api/queue and GET /api/queue/:filmId answer without a passcode and without CORS headers
Films still in status 'new' at boot are re-submitted oldest first; films in other statuses are left alone; a missing director module only logs
The only edit outside owned files is the appended installFilmQueue entry in server/boot.ts

stories.title: web/src/panels/QueueBanner.tsx: show a waiting film its place in line
stories.description: As a judge whose film is waiting for the crew, I want to see my place in line and a rough wait so that I know it has not hung.
steps: Read web/src/panels/Storyboard.tsx and web/src/panels/NewFilm.tsx (S3b), the film state hook (useFilm, S2) and web/src/api (typed fetch helpers).

Create web/src/panels/QueueBanner.tsx exporting QueueBanner(props: {filmId: string; status: FilmState['status']; pollMs?: number; fetchImpl?: typeof fetch}). It renders nothing unless status is 'new'. While status is 'new' it fetches GET /api/queue/<filmId> immediately and then every pollMs (default 5000) and clears the interval on unmount and when status changes. For {state: 'queued'} render `Waiting for the crew: #<position> in line, about <max(1, ceil(etaSec / 60))> min (estimate)`; for 'running' render `Starting the crew…`; for 'unknown' or a failed fetch render nothing. Use role='status' and aria-live='polite', existing CSS tokens only, no new dependency.

Edit web/src/panels/Storyboard.tsx (a named shared edit: the file belongs to S3b): add one import and one `<QueueBanner filmId={film.id} status={film.status} />` line at the top of the panel's render, where the film state is already available. If Storyboard.tsx does not exist or has no film status in scope, set this story's notes to 'blocked: no place to mount the banner' and stop; do not edit App.tsx.

Create web/src/panels/QueueBanner.test.tsx (jsdom, fake timers, a fake fetch): queued shows '#2 in line' and 'about 4 min' for etaSec 200; running shows the starting text; status 'planning' renders nothing and makes no request; the banner polls again after pollMs while 'new' and stops polling after the status changes; unknown renders nothing.
acceptance: A film in status 'new' that the queue reports as queued at position 2 with etaSec 200 shows 'Waiting for the crew: #2 in line, about 4 min (estimate)'
A film in any other status renders nothing and sends no request; polling stops when the status changes or the component unmounts
The only edit outside owned files is one import and one line in web/src/panels/Storyboard.tsx

stories.title: Dockerfile and .dockerignore
stories.description: As an operator, I want a container recipe with ffmpeg so that the server can run on a small machine.
steps: Read package.json (scripts and engines), server/main.ts and server/http/static.ts (S2), and docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md sections 3.4 and 10. If package.json has no 'start' script, add "start": "tsx server/main.ts" (S2-owned file; one additive line; record in notes).

Create deploy/Dockerfile (multi-stage): build stage FROM node:22-bookworm-slim AS build, WORKDIR /app, COPY package.json package-lock.json ./, RUN npm ci, COPY . ., RUN npm run build. Runtime stage FROM node:22-bookworm-slim: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ffmpeg ca-certificates && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*, WORKDIR /app, ENV NODE_ENV=production PORT=8080, COPY --from=build /app /app, EXPOSE 8080, CMD ["npm", "start"]. The container runs as root because Fly volumes mount root-owned (design section 10).
Create .dockerignore at the repository root excluding: node_modules, .git, .env, .env.*, data, debug, .ralph-tui, docs, web/dist, dist, *.log, .DS_Store.
Create deploy/dockerfile.test.ts that reads both files as text and asserts the lines below (no docker is run).
acceptance: The Dockerfile's first FROM is 'node:22-bookworm-slim' and it installs ffmpeg with apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends
'COPY package.json package-lock.json' appears before 'COPY . .' (dependency layer caching) and the Dockerfile sets ENV PORT=8080 and a CMD that starts the server
No Dockerfile line copies a .env file or sets an ENV or ARG whose name contains KEY, TOKEN or PASSCODE
.dockerignore lists .env, data, debug, node_modules and .ralph-tui

stories.title: fly.toml with verified keys
stories.description: As an operator, I want a Fly config in the repo so that deploying is one command and teardown is predictable.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md sections 3.4, 11 (V6) and 12, deploy/Dockerfile, and server/env.ts (S2) for how booleans and DATA_DIR are parsed.

Create fly.toml at the repository root (Fly's default location, so fly deploy finds it) with: app = "pixitween-director" with a comment to rename it; primary_region = "iad"; [build] dockerfile = "deploy/Dockerfile"; [env] PORT = "8080", NODE_ENV = "production", DATA_DIR = "/data", TRUST_FLY_CLIENT_IP set to the truthy form that server/env.ts accepts (read its parser; "true" unless it says otherwise), PUBLIC_BASE_URL = "https://pixitween-director.fly.dev" (comment: change with the app name); [http_service] internal_port = 8080, force_https = true, auto_stop_machines = "off", auto_start_machines = true, min_machines_running = 1; [[http_service.checks]] grace_period = "20s", interval = "30s", method = "GET", timeout = "5s", path = "/api/health"; [[vm]] cpu_kind = "shared", cpus = 1, memory = "1gb"; [mounts] source = "director_data", destination = "/data", initial_size = "1gb" (the volume is mounted at /data and DATA_DIR points the stores at it; Fly documents destination as any path other than "/").
Add comments: secrets are set with fly secrets and never listed here; auto_stop is off during judging 5 to 16 Nov 2026.
Create deploy/fly-config.test.ts asserting the keys by regular expressions on the file text (no TOML parser dependency); TRUST_FLY_CLIENT_IP must match /TRUST_FLY_CLIENT_IP = "(true|1)"/.
acceptance: The file contains primary_region = "iad", dockerfile = "deploy/Dockerfile", internal_port = 8080, auto_stop_machines = "off", min_machines_running = 1 and path = "/api/health"
It contains destination = "/data" and source = "director_data" in the [mounts] table, and [env] sets DATA_DIR = "/data"
No line sets META_API_KEY, CLIPPY_TOKEN, CLIPPY_MCP_URL or DIRECTOR_PASSCODE

stories.title: Pre-deploy check script
stories.description: As an operator, I want a script that scans the build and deploy files for leaked keys so that a mistake is caught before the deploy.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md sections 10 and 7, deploy/Dockerfile, .dockerignore and fly.toml.

Create deploy/predeploy-check.ts exporting scanForKeys(text: string): Array<{ pattern: string; index: number }> and checkDeploy(root: string): { errors: string[]; warnings: string[] }, and a main guard that prints them and exits 1 on errors (never at module load in tests).

scanForKeys flags: /sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}/, /Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{20,}/, /(META_API_KEY|CLIPPY_TOKEN|DIRECTOR_PASSCODE)\s*[:=]\s*['"]?[A-Za-z0-9]/, and the bare name 'META_API_KEY' (a server-only variable must not appear in web bundles).

checkDeploy: error when web/dist/index.html is missing; error for any scanForKeys hit in a text file under web/dist, deploy/Dockerfile or fly.toml; error when .dockerignore lacks '.env' or 'data'; warning when fly.toml still has app = "pixitween-director" (rename it).
Create deploy/predeploy-check.test.ts with temp directories.
acceptance: scanForKeys('Authorization: Bearer abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123') returns one hit and scanForKeys('Bearer short') returns none
scanForKeys('const x = "META_API_KEY"') returns a hit (name present in a bundle)
checkDeploy on a temp root without web/dist/index.html returns an error mentioning 'web/dist/index.html'
checkDeploy on a clean temp root reports the 'rename the app' warning and no errors

stories.title: Static serving integration test
stories.description: As an operator, I want a test that proves the server serves the built web app and an SPA fallback so that the container shows the UI.
steps: Read server/http/static.ts and server/main.ts (S2) to see how the static handler is created and which root it reads, and docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md section 3.4.

Create server/http/static.integration.test.ts: build a temp directory with index.html (text '<!doctype html><title>t</title>') and assets/app.js ('console.log(1)'), point the static handler at it (pass the root if static.ts accepts one, otherwise chdir into a temp tree that has web/dist), mount it the way main.ts does on a Hono app that also has GET /api/ping returning { ok: true } and an /api catch-all returning 404 JSON, and assert the behaviour below.
If a case fails because static.ts lacks it, make the smallest additive fix in server/http/static.ts (S2-owned) and record it in notes.
acceptance: GET / returns 200 with the index.html text
GET /some/client/route (no file) returns 200 with the index.html text (SPA fallback)
GET /assets/app.js returns 200 with a javascript content type and the file text
GET /api/ping returns the JSON, and GET /api/missing returns 404 JSON and not index.html

stories.title: Theme tokens for light and dark
stories.description: As a visitor, I want consistent light and dark colours so that the demo is readable in either system theme.
steps: Read web/src/main.tsx and web/index.html (S2) and docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md section 12 and requirements FR-8.

Create web/src/styles/theme.css defining the same custom properties in light and dark: --bg, --fg, --muted, --card, --border, --accent, --danger, --radius, --space-1 to --space-4. Light values in :root; dark values inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme="light"]) { ... } } and again in :root[data-theme="dark"]. Set color-scheme: light dark, and body { background: var(--bg); color: var(--fg); }.
Add one import line for the stylesheet in web/src/main.tsx (S2-owned; record in notes).

Create web/src/styles/theme.test.ts that reads the CSS text, extracts the custom property names from the light block and the dark blocks, and computes WCAG contrast between --fg and --bg for both modes with a small helper in the test file.
acceptance: The set of custom property names in the light block equals the set in the dark @media block and in the [data-theme="dark"] block
The contrast ratio of --fg on --bg is at least 4.5 in light mode and at least 4.5 in dark mode
web/src/main.tsx imports './styles/theme.css'

stories.title: Responsive layout pass at 375 px
stories.description: As a visitor on a phone, I want the app to fit a 375 px screen so that I can browse the gallery and watch a film without horizontal scrolling.
steps: Read web/src/App.tsx, web/src/styles/theme.css and the panels' class names (web/src/panels/*.tsx) to see the layout, and docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md sections 9 and 12.

Create web/src/styles/responsive.css and import it from web/src/main.tsx after theme.css (record the one-line edit in notes). Rules: *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box }; html, body { margin: 0 }; img, video, canvas, svg { max-width: 100%; height: auto }; the app's grid container becomes a single column below 768 px with min-width: 0 on its children; pre, code, td { overflow-wrap: anywhere }. Do not use overflow-x: hidden on html or body to hide overflow.

Start the dev server, then with the browser tools set the viewport to 375 x 812 (resize_window mobile preset) and check three states: no film loaded, the fixture film loaded (?fixture=1), and the gallery. Do the same at 1280 px, and in light and dark colour schemes. Record document.documentElement.scrollWidth and window.innerWidth for each state in notes.
If a panel component forces overflow with fixed pixel widths, do not edit it (other steps own those files); list the file and line in notes.
acceptance: At 375 px, document.documentElement.scrollWidth is less than or equal to window.innerWidth in all three states (values recorded in notes)
At 1280 px the layout is unchanged: no panel overlaps another (screenshot described in notes)
Text is readable in both colour schemes (no text with contrast below the theme tokens' 4.5:1 ratio)
responsive.css contains no 'overflow-x: hidden' on html or body

stories.title: deploy/README.md: owner commands and teardown
stories.description: As an owner, I want exact deploy and teardown commands in one place so that I can ship on Monday and leave nothing billing after the vote.
steps: Read fly.toml, deploy/Dockerfile, deploy/predeploy-check.ts and docs/hackathon/steps/step-08-export-and-deploy/design.md sections 8, 9, 11 (V6, V7) and 12.

Create deploy/README.md with these level-2 headings in order: Prerequisites, Pre-deploy checks, Create the app, Secrets, Deploy, Verify, Seed the gallery, Teardown. Prerequisites: flyctl installed and logged in, a payment method, the owner prices a shared-cpu-1x machine with 1 GB RAM and a 1 GB volume on Fly's pricing page before approving (state no number).

Commands (verified flags only): npm ci, npm run build, npx tsx deploy/predeploy-check.ts; optional local container test docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile -t pixitween-director . then docker run with port 8080 and a data volume; fly launch --no-deploy --copy-config --name <app> --region iad; fly volumes create director_data --region iad --size 1 -a <app>; fly secrets set with META_API_KEY, DIRECTOR_PASSCODE, CLIPPY_MCP_URL and CLIPPY_TOKEN placeholders and a note to run fly secrets set --help to confirm the syntax; fly deploy; fly status and fly logs.

Verify: how to request /api/health on the app's URL and the expected JSON, open the gallery in a private window, make a film with the passcode, and confirm the 4th film from one IP within an hour gets a 429. Seed the gallery: how to run npx tsx scripts/seed-gallery.ts inside the machine with DATA_DIR=/data (mark the fly ssh console syntax as unverified).

Teardown, to run on or after Mon 16 Nov 2026 (the community vote result): fly apps destroy <app> -y, then fly volumes list -a <app> and fly apps list to confirm nothing remains; say that whether apps destroy removes volumes is unverified, so destroy any remaining volume explicitly. Add a line: set a calendar reminder for 16 Nov 2026.
Create deploy/readme.test.ts asserting the headings, the strings 'fly apps destroy' and '--no-deploy' and '16 Nov 2026', and that scanForKeys(readmeText) returns no hits.

In deploy/README.md add a short 'Tuning the crew' section: the four admission variables (FILMS_IN_FLIGHT_MAX 2, FILMS_QUEUE_MAX 4, FILMS_STARTS_PER_WINDOW 3, FILMS_WINDOW_SEC 300), what each does, that the Meta key allows 150 requests per window (window length unpublished) and a film is budgeted at 40, and how to read x-ratelimit-remaining-requests to recalibrate; list them under the `fly secrets`/env section of fly.toml as optional overrides.
acceptance: deploy/README.md has the eight level-2 headings in the stated order
It contains 'fly launch --no-deploy --copy-config', 'fly volumes create director_data', 'fly apps destroy' and the date '16 Nov 2026'
scanForKeys(readmeText) returns an empty array (no key-like strings)
The Secrets section lists placeholders such as <your key> and never a real value
